categories.label: Airband
categories.blurb: Civil aviation voice: VHF AM (118–137 MHz, line-of-sight, so you need a receiver near an airport) and long-range HF upper-sideband for oceanic traffic. Gander Radio runs the North Atlantic right next to PEI.
categories.legal: Listening is fine; in Canada do not record-and-share or act on what you hear (Radiocommunication Act s.9(2)).

categories.label: Marine
categories.blurb: Maritime distress & calling, Coast Guard broadcasts and the HF safety channels. NAVTEX and AIS are data — you will hear tones/bursts; dedicated decoders show the text/ship positions.
categories.legal: Distress and safety channels are fine to monitor; ship-to-ship conversations are private comms — don't divulge them.

categories.label: ADS-B
categories.blurb: Aircraft broadcast their own position on 1090 MHz. The Flights tab shows it live from the public adsb.fi network; some OpenWebRX receivers decode it too. With your own RTL-SDR you can feed the network.

presets.plain: A second position-broadcast channel used by smaller aircraft in the United States.

categories.plain: ADS-B = the signal planes broadcast automatically with their position, height and speed.

categories.label: ACARS / HFDL
categories.blurb: Aircraft text datalinks: VHF ACARS (AM bursts near 129–131 MHz) and HF Data Link (HFDL). Here you can hear and identify the signal; decoders such as acarsdec / dumphfdl turn it into text.
categories.legal: ACARS messages are addressed to airlines. In Canada treat their content as private: identifying the signal is fine, but don't log, publish or use message contents.

categories.blurb: Automatic Packet Reporting System — hams beaconing position, weather stations and messages as 1200-baud packets. Fully public; aprs.fi maps every packet heard by internet gateways.

categories.label: Satellites
categories.blurb: Weather and amateur satellites passing overhead. Meteor-M LRPT (137 MHz) sends cloud imagery; the ISS does occasional SSTV and voice on 145.800. NOAA-15/18/19 APT was retired in 2025. Passes last ~12 min — check a pass predictor first.

categories.label: Numbers (ref)
categories.blurb: Reference only. "Numbers stations" are one-way shortwave broadcasts of spoken digits or data, widely believed to be for intelligence services. Schedules shift constantly — check Priyom, then tune any HF receiver to the listed time and frequency.
categories.plain: Mysterious stations that read out strings of spoken numbers, widely believed to be coded messages for spies. Reference only — nothing to tune here.
